items.title: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum Interview, 1960-10-16
items.q: Yeah, because my brother would have been a famous musician anyway.

ctx.x: I hope because I hope he got too good of it.

Yeah, because my brother would have been a famous musician anyway. Yes, he must have. He was a wonderful trumpet musician. He was famous when he was in the middle. He was famous. If he could hold a note, you're talking about Louis Armstrong holding a note. But little George could hold that note. And I'm sure he would have been real famous. He was only 32 when he died.

Only 32. Yes. He used to play with Henry Jr. or I said, but it's Clare that same, the fine Clare that same woman on the music box. But George was playing that legit dance on Crandelet and Canal. Right on that call. Yeah, he played seven years. He cut a record. He was working every day when he was playing a really bad night.
